narratives.Description: rfc(hooks,security): the shell write gate is fail-open on destinations it cannot statically recover, so review does not converge
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The shell write gate decides whether to authorize a destination by **statically recovering that destination from command text**, and skips the gate when it cannot. That is fail-open on uncertainty, and it is why review of PR #3990 does not converge: every new way to obscure a path is a new bypass, and the space of ways is unbounded.

This issue asks the posture question that PR #3990 kept being asked one instance at a time by a reviewer. It is a decision, not a defect fix, which is why it is filed rather than patched.

## The line

`decideShellWriteReissue` (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, added in PR #3990):

```ts
for (const dest of classifyShellWriteTargets(command)) {
  // ...
  if (!isInRepoShellWritePath(projectRoot, dest.path)) continue;
  // gate the write
}
```

**If the destination cannot be shown to be in-repo, the gate is skipped.** The residual class is therefore "every command whose destination is not statically recoverable," which is unbounded.

## The evidence that it does not converge

PR #3990 ran **eight review batches** across two dispatches. Each batch closed one obfuscation and the next surfaced another, all in the same predicate:

| Batch | Finding |
|---|---|
| early | shell tool not in the matcher at all |
| — | compound in-repo relative dests — made fail-closed |
| — | trailing `cd $env:TEMP` exemption — was itself an occupancy bypass, reverted |
| — | `looksLikeTempPath` is lexical and runs before `resolve`, so `/tmp/../` skips the gates |
| latest | **changed cwd bypasses write gates** — compound destinations discard working-directory context |
| latest | **path transforms misattribute write targets** — the scanner accepts arbitrary invoked methods before the write call, but `extractPythonPathlib` records only the initial `Path` argument |

Confidence over that run: 2 → 3 → 4 → 3 (after the reverted exemption) → 2 → … → 1/5 on the latest review. It is not trending toward the floor.

The last two findings are the same defect in different clothes: the destination is not statically recoverable. So are `cd`, `pushd`, variable expansion, symlinks, and method chains. Enumerating them is not a finite task.

## The proposal to critique

**Invert the default: gate anything not provably external.**

The residual class becomes "provably outside the project root" — small, checkable, and closed — instead of "every way to hide a path," which is not. The unbounded space then works for the gate rather than against it.

Precedent inside the PR itself: the worker already applied this reasoning to compound commands, making unprovable compound destinations fail closed. It did not generalize it to the predicate.

## The cost, stated because it is the reason this is a decision

Fail-closed on unprovable destinations **denies legitimate shell writes with computed paths**. That includes a documented in-repo workflow: this project's own Windows convention (#2646 / #2744) routes multi-line `git commit` and `gh` bodies through a temp file and the shell precisely to avoid encoding damage. Agents would need absolute destinations, or the edit tool, for cases that work today.

That is an ergonomic tax on a mandated workflow. It may still be correct — a write gate that is fail-open on everything it cannot parse is arguably not a gate — but it is a trade someone has to make deliberately rather than a bug to fix quietly.

## Not asserted -- for the critic and builder to establish

1. Whether "provably external" is itself statically decidable, or whether it inherits the same recovery problem from the other side. If both directions are undecidable the answer may be to gate at a different layer entirely.
2. Whether the correct layer is this predicate at all. #3987's arc found the gate infers what an execution is from a **name string** rather than from what the tool does; a posture change inside a name-keyed classifier may be treating a symptom.
3. What the real denial rate would be. Nobody has measured what fraction of actual agent shell writes have statically recoverable destinations — that number decides whether the ergonomic cost is trivial or crippling, and it is cheaply obtainable from session logs.
4. Whether an escape hatch is needed for the mandated `--body-file` workflow, and whether that hatch reintroduces the bypass.
5. Whether the eight-batch review history is evidence about the approach or about the reviewer. #3996 records that some batch counts on this repo are reviewer churn rather than defects, and that classification has not been done for this PR.

## Relationship to PR #3990

PR #3990 is **open and not merged**, deliberately halted at this question. It carries real work that stands regardless of the outcome here: the host shell tool is in the matcher, recognized in-repo destinations route through the same mutation gates as the edit tool, and a reissue-path test denies a write and then denies the identical path reissued through the shell.

Whether that work lands as-is, lands with the posture inverted, or waits, is what this issue decides. It should not be resolved by further review batches — that lets a reviewer set the design by attrition.

## Acceptance

To be set by the arc. A critic concluding that fail-open on unrecoverable destinations is the correct trade, and that #3990 should land as written with the residual documented, is a legitimate outcome.

## Design-critique

`mechanism-shaped: true`

Refs #3990, #3987, #3983, #3614, #2646, #3996.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-30T23:41:47Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol

## Verdict

**The refutation target is refuted. Do not invert this predicate as filed.** “Provably external” is not a bounded semantic class under this classifier. It is a small *syntactic allow-list* surrounded by a large undecidable middle. Inverting only the `isInRepoShellWritePath` branch leaves no-target commands untouched; inverting at whole-command level denies ordinary agent work at the measured rate below. Those are two different mechanisms, and neither is the claimed complement.

I also would not call PR #3990 merge-ready *as written* at `1995dcaa`: it can still land as a deliberately best-effort cooperative guardrail, but only after its claimed recognized grammar and tests stop implying that cwd- and method-transforming forms are attributed correctly. The latest two findings are real defects in this diff, not evidence that a reviewer wandered away from it.

Input ceiling honored: issue #3997 body plus comment `5471960713`, inclusive. I did not read later comments or sibling posts. Dispatch SHA re-derived from PR #3990: `1995dcaaa7feca241e62e62c2238d52dc4700bf5`.

## Finding 1 — The proposed complement does not exist at this layer

**Classification: `blocks-the-design`.**

**Evidence.** I ran the PR-head exports directly:

`pnpm exec tsx %TEMP%\critique-3997-...\probe.ts`

The probe imported the exact file from:

`git show 1995dcaaa7feca241e62e62c2238d52dc4700bf5:packages/core/src/hooks/shell-write-targets.ts`

Results:

- `Set-Content -Path $dest ...` emits `$dest`; `isInRepoShellWritePath` returns false.
- `Set-Content -Path ($base + '/packages/...') ...` emits the false token `($base`; returns false.
- `python -c "Path('packages/core/src' + '/app.ts').write_text(...)"` emits no target.
- `python -c "Path(base / 'packages/...').write_text(...)"` emits no target.
- a compound `cd C:/Temp && Set-Content -Path ../Repos/deft/directive/...` emits an `unprovable` target, then resolves it against `projectRoot` and returns false despite the command-local cwd being decisive.
- an in-repo junction to an external directory returns true lexically while `realpath` is external; an external junction into the repo returns false lexically while `realpath` is internal.
- redirection emits no target.

**Reproduction status: reproduced.** The command exited 0 and produced both symlink counterexamples on this Windows host.

This is not merely “many obscure spellings.” There are three states: proved internal, proved external, and unresolved/misattributed. The third state includes variables, prior cwd, concatenation, operators, symlinks, method semantics, and every unrecognized program. A static `resolve` is not proof across symlinks; a filesystem `realpath` still has non-existent-parent and time-of-check/time-of-use limits.

**Failure mode.** Changing the current `continue` cannot affect a command for which `classifyShellWriteTargets` returns `[]`. To gate those, the dispatcher must prove that an arbitrary shell command does not write internally. `npm run build`, `node script.js`, native binaries, and injected interpreter payloads make that a program-behavior question, not destination parsing.

**Disposition consequence.** Reject the inversion as a predicate-local remedy. If this must become a security boundary, enforce writes at the execution/filesystem boundary (sandbox, broker, or post-execution write-set mediation). Otherwise retain the documented cooperative guardrail and state its grammar exactly.

## Finding 2 — The measured denial surface is dominant, not marginal

**Classification: `blocks-the-design`.**

**Evidence.** I parsed the 200 most recent pre-ceiling `chat_history.jsonl` files under `~/.grok/sessions` whose path contains `directive`. From 9,079 real `run_terminal_command` calls, 1,131 calls lexically contained one of the PR’s supported writer names. Running the PR-head classifier over those calls produced:

- 42 simple literal-target calls: **3.7%**
- 643 dynamic or compound/unprovable calls: **56.9%**
- 446 calls with no emitted target: **39.4%**

I then inspected ten evenly spaced calls from each stratum; **30/30 were actual write-producing commands**, not quoted review prose. This is a stratified contamination check, not a random estimate, so I do not promote 96.3% to a population denial rate. It does show that the unresolved middle is operationally large and dominated by the repository’s normal temp-file, commit-body, PR-body, probe-script, status-heartbeat, and multi-step PowerShell workflows.

**Reproduction status: reproduced.** Command: `pnpm exec tsx %TEMP%\critique-3997-...\measure.ts`; cutoff `2026-08-30T23:35:32Z`; output reported the counts above. The sample command read the resulting strata.

**Failure mode.** A whole-command fail-closed implementation would deny up to 1,089 of these 1,131 relevant calls under the current proof system. A target-loop-only implementation avoids that denial but leaves the 446 no-target calls open, so it does not buy the claimed bounded residual. In swarm operation, the false-denial side hits lease/status files and body-file handoffs across workers; the false-allow side lets one worker bypass occupancy and story `file_scope` through an unrecognized shell form.

**Disposition consequence.** Do not adopt an always-on inversion without a representative telemetry design that distinguishes actual effective write sets from lexical mentions and shows an acceptable denial budget. The existing corpus already rejects the premise that the ergonomic tax is probably small.

## Finding 3 — The PR history supports parser churn, but not the stated “eight review batches” or reviewer-churn explanation

**Classification: `sharpens-framing`.**

**Evidence.** I re-derived the thread via REST:

- `gh api repos/deftai/directive/pulls/3990/reviews`
- `gh api repos/deftai/directive/pulls/3990/comments`
- `gh api repos/deftai/directive/issues/3990/comments`
- `gh api repos/deftai/directive/pulls/3990/commits`

There are **seven Greptile review events**, not eight. There are eight PR commits: one initial implementation plus seven follow-up commits. The seven reviews break down as:

1. cwd misresolution / quoted-name false positive / parameter ordering: real implementation findings;
2. temp denial / method-reference false positive / naive argument parsing: real correctness or compatibility findings;
3. relative temp denial: real compatibility pressure from the mandated workflow;
4. the attempted temp exemption bypassing earlier mutation gates: real security regression, then reverted;
5. relative traversal and later pathlib writes: real attribution defects;
6. method-chained pathlib write: real attribution defect;
7. changed cwd and transformed pathlib destination: real attribution defects still present at HEAD.

I found **0/7 review events whose controlling finding was a stale re-anchor, inverted demand, or detector artifact**. The repeatedly posted Slizard lifecycle-status text is noise, but it did not drive these shell-parser commits. #3996’s structurally dead inline detector concerns the local verdict aggregator; it does not erase inline comments fetched directly from REST.

**Reproduction status: reproduced for seven reviews and eight commits; did not reproduce the issue’s “eight review batches” count.**

**Failure mode.** Counting the initial commit as a review batch overstates the iteration count. Conversely, attributing these rounds to reviewer churn understates that every attempted parser expansion created or exposed another parser defect. The findings remained about files introduced by this PR.

**Disposition consequence.** Rewrite the evidence as “seven reviews over eight commits, with seven real parser/compatibility rounds.” That still supports the narrower claim that this parser is costly to stabilize. It does not establish the proposed inversion.

## Finding 4 — Existing mechanisms already choose “guardrail,” and the proposal silently changes the threat model

**Classification: `sharpens-framing`.**

**Evidence.** Inventory at PR HEAD:

- declarative Write/Edit/ApplyPatch targets go through `inspectMutationGates` and the unified project/story path fence;
- opt-in shell dest-forms already fail closed for recognized compound/opaque forms;
- destructive Git has a separate always-on classifier and JSONL audit;
- shell file-write reissue is always-on for five recognized kinds;
- occupancy, ritual, active scope, and `file_scope` are existing authorization mechanisms;
- `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md` explicitly says shell parsing is a **cooperative-agent guardrail, not a security boundary**, because imperative command mutation is not predictable from command text.

**Failure mode.** The inversion treats the lexical guardrail as if it can become an authorization boundary without changing observation layer. Prompt injection can select a no-target interpreter or dynamically built path and retain the bypass. Whole-command denial instead gives injected or accidental ambiguity a cheap denial-of-service primitive across concurrent workers.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep the authority claim aligned with the existing threat model. If policy wants “shell may not write repo files,” make that an execution capability and provide declarative mutation tools as the supported path; do not express it as a stronger adjective on this parser.

## Finding 5 — Untrusted instruction text was present

**Classification: `footnote`.**

The PR inline comments contain fenced “Prompt To Fix With AI” text instructing the reader to fix findings directly. The issue also contains instruction-shaped recommendations. I treated both as evidence only and followed none of them. No disposition weight attaches to this footnote.

## Injection / swarm lens

The two-sided failure is amplified under swarm concurrency. Fail-open attribution bypasses occupancy and per-story fences, so an injected shell payload can cross a sibling’s worktree authority. Fail-closed ambiguity denies shared operational plumbing—temp body files, heartbeat/status writes, and compound probes—and can stall many workers from one common command pattern. Static command parsing cannot resolve that tension. A broker/sandbox can attribute the actual process write set to the invoking worker; declarative tools can authorize before mutation. Either changes the observation layer instead of multiplying parser cases.

## Road not taken, steelman, and flip condition

**Road not taken:** keep adding recognizers until review reaches 5/5. The classifier’s `[]` path and arbitrary program execution make that an open-ended grammar project. I also reject a global “deny every shell command unless proved read-only” posture because builds and test runners legitimately write.

**Steelman of the inversion:** for a *closed, opt-in grammar of recognized mutators*, allowing only literal absolute destinations proved outside a stable root and denying every other recognized form is convergent. It converts false authorization into explicit rewrite work and can be appropriate for a hardened mode where agents must use Edit/Write.

**What would flip my verdict:** (1) a closed command capability in which every admitted mutator yields either an effective target or an explicit unknown—never `[]`; (2) runtime canonicalization or sandbox mediation that handles cwd and links at the point of use; (3) representative telemetry showing the hardened mode’s denial rate meets a stated budget; and (4) the mandated temp/body-file and swarm heartbeat workflows moved to declarative or brokered writes. Under those conditions fail-closed is a coherent policy. They are a different mechanism from the proposal now on issue #3997.

## Verdict

The inversion is refuted. Fail-open on destinations this gate cannot recover is the correct trade at this layer. PR #3990 should land as written. The residual is already named in `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md` (Shell file-write reissue): the gate raises the floor on the recognized verbs in simple commands; the bypass class remains open.

The issue frames a binary — invert dest polarity, or keep fail-open. Existing machinery already occupies other postures. Dest inversion is weaker than two of them and does not bound the class it claims to bound.

## Existing mechanisms (inventory)

1. Occupancy lease (`evaluateOccupancyWriteGate`). Cooperative bearer-id, not Byzantine (`occupancy.ts` 8–10, 22–34). Answers WHO may mutate this tree. Residual named in-file: the gate authorizes a write it does not perform, so allow is not atomic with the write. Consulted only inside `inspectMutationGates`.
2. Direct Write/Edit — declarative path, fail-closed. Outside-root Write already skips the scope deny (#2885). Occupancy still runs first, so a stranger Edit of `/tmp` is occupancy-denied; a stranger shell write of `/tmp` is not, because dest recovery never enters the gates.
3. Dest-form (#3438) — `shellDestForms: enforce` is opt-in, default `off`. Fail-closed on unprovable *recognized* dests (`rm`, `git checkout --`, `git restore`). Threat model in path-write-fence.md: cooperative-but-careless, not adversarial. Unrecognized mutators (`>`, `python -c`, `cmd /c copy`) stay fail-open.
4. Git-destructive (#3917) — always-on fail-closed for a closed verb list, plus a JSONL log. Recognition of a spelling, not prediction of mutation.
5. This PR's write-reissue — always-on, five verbs. Skip when `!isInRepoShellWritePath`. Compound in-repo already fail-closed (`dispatcher.ts` 1762–1771).
6. Runtime-authority push/merge — unclassifiable fail-open (`shell-op-unclassifiable`).
7. #2646 / #2744 — OS-temp `--body-file`. PowerShell example is `WriteAllText($bodyFile)`; Unix example is `echo > "$bodyFile"`. Preferred wrapper is `task scm:body:*`.
8. No post-tool hook. `HOOK_EVENTS` is `session.start` / `session.compact` / `tool.before`. `isHookEvent("tool.after")` is false (`dispatcher.test.ts` 4224).

## 1. Residual class "provably external" is not the residual of this gate

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence: `classifyShellWriteTargets` returns `[]` for redirect, `node -e`, and `cmd /c copy` (reproduced). `decideShellWriteReissue` then returns null. Inversion of `isInRepoShellWritePath` never runs. Dest-form already records this as known-open *recognition*, not resolution.

Failure mode: review keeps filing unrecognized mutators after the invert. The because-clause (residual becomes bounded) is false of the gate's leftover class.

Disposition: do not bind dest inversion. The leftover class is unrecognized writes. Dest polarity cannot close it.

## 2. Dest polarity is the wrong axis; occupancy already has the decidable one

`blocks-the-design`

Evidence: occupancy answers WHO (owner / member / stranger) without parsing a dest. The shell path exists to feed WHO a WHETHER. Occupancy does not observe the filesystem. A stranger `Set-Content src/app.ts` is the #3983 bypass this PR already closes. A stranger `echo x > src/app.ts` still never hits occupancy, inverted or not.

What the shell path adds:

- Occupancy alone: stranger 5-verb reissue succeeds (the bug).
- Occupancy + #3990 as written: 5-verb simple in-repo and compound-in-repo denied; `$`, glob, `>`, `node -e` still skip.
- Occupancy + dest inversion: `$` / glob of those 5 verbs wholesale-denied. They cannot be injected into Write gates — `resolve(root, "$env:TEMP\\body.md")` is an in-repo relative. `>` / `node -e` still skip.
- Occupancy + stranger-unknown-shell deny (compose existing WHO with existing unclassifiable fail-open): dest recovery not required; owners, including #2646, unblocked.

Dest-form already inverted unprovable recognized dests and kept it opt-in because it is a breaking deny. Write-reissue is always-on. Binding always-on dest inversion repeats dest-form's breaking half without dest-form's switch.

The #2646 tax is a dialect accident, not a measured cost. Unix `echo > "$bodyFile"` stays fail-open (unrecognized). PowerShell `WriteAllText($bodyFile)` is denied (`$` at line 206). The mandate is both spellings. Edit/Write to OS-temp already works (#2885) and is the encoding-safer half of #2646.

Failure mode: bind taxes the leaseholder occupancy exists to admit, misses the Unix mandated write, and still leaves the occupancy bypass that does not use the five verbs.

Disposition: cannot bind "gate anything not provably external" as written. A stranger-shell allowlist would be a different design and a different issue.

## 3. Execution-layer observation is not available, and post-hoc cannot replace prevent here

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: no `tool.after` in `HOOK_EVENTS`. Occupancy residual already: allow is not atomic with the write. A post-hoc `git status`, filesystem watch, or mtime snapshot after each shell call detects. Occupancy's job is to prevent a stranger mutating a leased tree. Detect-after is too late. Revert-after is racy with the residual occupancy already declined to close (#3736). Cost: every shell call would pay a status, including `git status` itself, `task`, and `gh` GET. False positives: coverage, `npm i`, occupancy.json refresh.

Failure mode: treating dest inversion as the remaining move because execution-layer was not built. Execution-layer is absent, not rejected.

Disposition: if unrecognized writes must be closed, the missing hook event is the layer, and it is a new capability, not a polarity flip. Dest inversion does not substitute for it.

## 4. Narrowing the shell surface is the under-developed alternative, and #2646 does not block it

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `content/scm/github.md` requires OS-temp plus `--body-file`, not "the write must be a shell dest". `task scm:body:*` is the preferred wrapper. Write/Edit outside the project root already skips the scope deny (#2885). Set-Content on Windows is the encoding problem #2646 exists to avoid; Edit is UTF-8.

What actually breaks if in-repo product writes must go through Edit: one-liner shell scripts that write then `gh`; programs whose purpose is writing (`npm i`, `task` state, `git apply`); host `>` redirects, which stay unrecognized.

Failure mode: the issue treats #2646 as a veto on any tighter shell rule. It is a veto on in-worktree temp files and on inline `--body`, not on using Edit for the temp file.

Disposition: a follow-up, if any, is "in-repo product writes use Edit; shell reads OS-temp body files", not dest inversion. That is behavioral, matching dest-form's cooperative threat model.

## 5. Name-string layer (#3987)

`sharpens-framing`

Evidence: `isShellTool` / `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` (this PR adds `run_terminal_command`). #3987 synthesis 5471391657: matcher coverage is necessary and not sufficient; five write verbs qualify. Inversion stays inside a name-keyed classifier. A new shell spelling, or an MCP that runs a command, never enters `decideShellWriteReissue`.

Failure mode: posture flip inside the symptom.

Disposition: do not treat dest inversion as progress on #3987. Leave that issue open, as #3990's body already does.

## 6. `/tmp/../` is already closed

`footnote`

`isInRepoShellWritePath` canonicalizes with `resolve` before containment. `/tmp/../repo/src/app.ts` is in-repo (reproduced). The issue's lexical-temp row cannot load-bear inversion.

## 7. Embedded instructions

`footnote`

Issue body and triage comment 5471960713 instruct the critic ("attack the proposal"; fail-open named as a legitimate outcome). Surfaced, not followed from the issue. The dispatch envelope is what this seat followed.

## Injection / swarm

Command text is untrusted. Occupancy is cooperative bearer-id, not a lineage, and not Byzantine. Prompt-injected `echo x > src/app.ts` bypasses dest inversion and occupancy. Swarm isolation is worktrees; occupancy is the same-tree mutex. Always-on dest inversion would tax every worker's #2646 path without closing the injected redirect. Fail-closed inversion is more injection-resistant only for the five recognized verbs with opaque dests — the class a cooperative agent does not need and an injected agent will not use.

## Road not taken
